title: A semisimple group has no nontrivial characters
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $X^*(G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{F\text{-grp}}(G,\mathbf G_m)$ for the abelian group of characters, with addition given by multiplication of values, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. A semisimple group means a smooth connected affine group of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme; solvable means that successive derived subgroup schemes eventually become trivial, where the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. For every semisimple group $H$, one has $X^*(H)=0$: every group-scheme homomorphism $H\to\mathbf G_m$ is the identity-valued homomorphism, after every scalar extension.

source.place: Corollary 21.50, printed p.440, together with Definition 12.45, printed p.245 (perfect means no nontrivial commutative quotient); also Remark 18.27, printed p.393.

proof.text: Fix a semisimple $H$ and a character $\chi:H\to\mathbf G_m$. The hypotheses in [lem-sfb-semisimple-group-perfect] agree with the stated definition of semisimple (smooth, connected, affine and finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup), so that node gives $H^{\mathrm{der}}=H$ as closed subgroup schemes, not merely an equality of rational-point groups.

source.place: Corollary 21.50, printed p.440; Definition 12.45, printed p.245

proof.text: The target $\mathbf G_m$ is affine, commutative and of finite type by [def-sc-gm-ga]: its coordinate ring is $F[t,t^{-1}]$ and its comultiplication $t\mapsto t\otimes t$ is invariant under swapping the tensor factors. The group $H$ is smooth and connected, so [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-derived-subgroup] applies to $\chi$ and says that $\chi$ restricts to the identity-valued homomorphism on $H^{\mathrm{der}}$. Substituting $H^{\mathrm{der}}=H$ from step 1 shows $\chi=e_{\mathbf G_m}\circ p_H$ as a morphism of group schemes, where $p_H:H\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is the structure map.

source.place: Proposition 6.18 and Corollary 6.19(d), printed p.129; smoothness qualification in Chapter 6 errata

proof.text: The identity-valued homomorphism exists, and the arbitrary character $\chi$ equals it, so the character group has exactly its zero element (addition of characters is multiplication of values). Equality here is equality of scheme morphisms: pulling the equality $\chi=e_{\mathbf G_m}\circ p_H$ back along any $F$-algebra $R$ yields $\chi_R=e_{\mathbf G_{m,R}}\circ p_{H_R}$, hence $\chi_R(A)(h)=1$ for every $R$-algebra $A$ and $h\in H_R(A)$. This proves the asserted triviality after every scalar extension without assuming that rational points detect morphisms.

source.place: Corollary 6.19(d), printed p.129 (arbitrary base algebra R); Definition 12.45, printed p.245

proof_origin.place: Corollary 21.50 and Definition 12.45, applied via Corollary 6.19(d)
